title: Zuri’s Rooftop Garden
credit: Original story and SVG illustrations created for Axiom Play Studios with OpenAI Codex.

scenes.narrative: Zuri follows Grandma through the rooftop door. A high, solid wall surrounds the roof, and Grandma stays with her. Beyond it rise windows, chimneys and the hum of the city. Inside is a cleared space for a garden. “We can use the long raised beds,” says Grandma, “or group these round pots.” Zuri studies the room each plan will make.
scenes.alt: A child with dark curly hair and a gold tunic stands with her silver-haired grandmother inside a rooftop garden enclosed by a high wall. City buildings rise beyond it; a workbench holds their plans.

options.label: Long raised beds
options.feedback: The long beds make one broad growing area. Zuri can work along their edges beside Grandma.

options.label: Groups of round pots
options.feedback: The pots make several small growing spaces. Grandma can move a pot when the arrangement changes.

scenes.narrative: A neighbour waves from the rooftop door. She would like to visit once the garden is growing. Zuri and Grandma have room for one main place to gather. A bench could hold a reader and a friend. A round table could hold cups and a drawing pad. Which kind of visit should this corner invite?
scenes.alt: Zuri and Grandma plan a visitor corner within the rooftop wall. There is space for a reading bench or a round table.

options.label: A reading bench for two
options.feedback: Grandma sets out a reading bench. A visitor can sit beside Zuri and share a book.

options.label: A family table for drawing
options.feedback: Grandma sets out the family table. Visitors can gather around cups, paper and pencils.

scenes.narrative: On the workbench sit young flower plants and sturdy little herb plants. Grandma has chosen varieties suited to this roof, and she will help give either group the care it needs. Flowers will bring colour and nectar for butterflies. Herbs will bring leaves to smell and, with Grandma’s help, use in food; small herb flowers can feed visiting bees too. They will not grow in a moment: days and regular care must pass.
scenes.alt: Young plants wait in an enclosed rooftop nursery. The child and grandmother compare colourful flower plants with leafy herbs before planting.

options.label: Colourful flower plants
options.feedback: They plant the young flowers. Over the coming days, Grandma helps water them and buds begin to open. A butterfly visits for nectar.

options.label: Fragrant leafy herbs
options.feedback: They plant the herbs. Over the coming days, Grandma helps water them and fresh leaves begin to grow. A bee visits the little herb flowers.

scenes.narrative: The visitors’ corner catches a warm patch of light. Grandma checks the plants; their growing space has the light each kind needs. This next choice is for the people resting nearby. A cloth can shade the seats now. Or they can leave the corner sunny and plan their visits for the cooler morning. They can still change the resting shade later.
scenes.alt: A sunny visitor corner lies inside the rooftop wall. Grandma can attach a shade cloth to secure posts; the plant area remains separate.

options.label: Hang the resting shade cloth
options.feedback: Grandma secures the shade cloth over the resting corner. Visitors can rest in its soft shade.

options.label: Leave the corner sunny
options.feedback: The corner stays sunny. Zuri plans cool morning visits and keeps a folded parasol nearby for later.

scenes.narrative: Grandma lays out flat stepping stones on the firm roof surface. Zuri traces a route with one finger. A looping path would let a visitor walk past more leaves. A straight path would make a shorter trip from the doorway to the seats. Both stay clear of the plants and leave room to walk beside Grandma.
scenes.alt: Flat stepping stones wait on the garden floor. Zuri and Grandma can arrange a broad loop past the plants or a short straight route to the seats.

options.label: Loop past the growing plants
options.feedback: The stones make a looping route. Visitors can pause by several plants on their way to the seats.

options.label: Go straight to the seats
options.feedback: The stones make a short, straight route. Visitors can reach the seats with fewer steps.

scenes.narrative: Several days pass. Zuri and Grandma return to care for the garden, and new growth appears. They can set a slow drip from Grandma’s covered water tank; while she fits it, Grandma can also open the folded parasol if the seats are still sunny. Or they can keep their morning watering-can routine, visiting the garden before the day grows warm. Grandma manages the water in either plan.
scenes.alt: After several days of care, the enclosed rooftop has fresh growth. Grandma offers a covered tank and drip hose, with a folded parasol available, or a watering can for morning visits.

options.label: Set a drip and add shade if needed
options.feedback: Grandma sets a slow drip for the plants. If the corner was sunny, she opens the parasol so visitors have shade too.

options.label: Water together in the cool morning
options.feedback: Zuri keeps the morning watering-can visits with Grandma. They check the soil and rest before the day grows warm.

scenes.narrative: More days pass with Grandma’s steady care. Between the city windows, Zuri’s rooftop has become a place to grow and visit. The chosen plants, insect visitors, seats, light, path and water plan belong to the same garden. Zuri shows the neighbour around. “We made room for the kind of visits we imagined,” she says.
scenes.alt: Within a high rooftop wall, a child and grandmother stand in their chosen garden: beds or pots, flowers with a butterfly or herbs with a bee after days of growth, a bench or table, a clear path, the selected resting shade and water plan.

prompts.question: Did the plants grow as soon as Zuri chose them?
prompts.answer: No. Days passed, and Zuri and Grandma kept caring for the plants.

prompts.question: Who managed the water and helped with the shade?
prompts.answer: Grandma managed the water and helped make the resting shade.

prompts.question: How might a neighbour feel arriving in this garden?
prompts.answer: They might feel curious, peaceful, welcome or something else. Look at your garden and share an idea.

prompts.question: Would you choose a reading visit or a drawing visit?
prompts.answer: Your preference is welcome. Tell someone what you would bring to the visit.
